generic: Liposomal Amphotericin B (Amphotericin B, liposomal - AmBisome)
quick: 3-5 mg/kg IV once daily (indication-dependent), infused over about 2 hours
May be used when benefit outweighs risk; preferred amphotericin form in pregnancy
Limited data; generally avoided or used with caution
Less nephrotoxic than conventional amphotericin but still monitor renal function
Monitor liver function; caution in hepatic impairment
Not directly relevant; avoid in unstable patients
Renal function, electrolytes (K, Mg), LFTs, CBC, infusion reactions
summary: Liposomal amphotericin B is a polyene antifungal in which amphotericin B is incorporated into liposomes, reducing nephrotoxicity and infusion reactions compared with conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate while preserving broad antifungal activity. It is used for serious systemic fungal infections, empirical therapy in febrile neutropenia, cryptococcal meningitis in HIV, and visceral leishmaniasis. Different amphotericin B products are NOT interchangeable on a mg-per-mg basis.
indications: Empirical therapy for presumed fungal infection in febrile neutropenic patients
Treatment of cryptococcal meningitis in HIV-infected patients
Treatment of Aspergillus, Candida and/or Cryptococcus infections refractory to or precluding conventional amphotericin B

dosage.n: Per label; combine per guideline (e.g. with flucytosine)

dosage.d: 3 mg/kg/day on days 1-5, and days 14 and 21 (total 21 mg/kg)
dosage.n: Immunocompromised regimens use higher cumulative dose

admin: Reconstitute and dilute per label; use a 5% dextrose diluent (not saline) for the final infusion
Administer by IV infusion over approximately 120 minutes using a controlled device
An in-line filter may be used only if pore diameter is not less than 1.0 micron
Flush existing IV lines with 5% dextrose before infusion; do not mix with other drugs
A test dose may be given; have support available for infusion reactions
moa: Amphotericin B binds preferentially to ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming pores that increase membrane permeability, cause leakage of intracellular potassium and other contents, and lead to fungal cell death. The liposomal carrier alters tissue distribution and reduces binding to mammalian cholesterol-containing membranes (especially renal), lowering nephrotoxicity while retaining fungicidal activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to amphotericin B or any component (unless desensitised when no alternative)

preg: Amphotericin B (including liposomal) is generally considered the antifungal of choice for serious systemic fungal infections in pregnancy when treatment is required, as it crosses the placenta minimally and has reassuring data; use when benefit outweighs risk.
lact: Limited data on excretion into breast milk. Poor oral absorption suggests low infant systemic exposure, but use with caution; weigh benefit against risk.
renal: Significantly less nephrotoxic than conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate, but renal impairment and electrolyte wasting can still occur. Monitor creatinine, potassium and magnesium; ensure hydration and replace electrolytes as needed.
hepatic: Hepatic dysfunction and raised liver enzymes can occur. Monitor liver function during therapy and use with caution in pre-existing hepatic impairment.

major: Other nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, cisplatin - additive renal toxicity)
moderate: Drugs whose toxicity rises with hypokalaemia (e.g. some antiarrhythmics)
minor: Flucytosine (enhanced antifungal effect but increased flucytosine toxicity if renal function falls)
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate creatinine, BUN, liver enzymes; lowers serum potassium and magnesium

monitoring: Vital signs during infusion for reactions
counsel: This medicine is given through a vein over about two hours in hospital
Tell staff right away about fever, chills, breathlessness, or rash during the infusion
Blood tests will check your kidneys, salts, and blood counts
Drink fluids as advised to protect the kidneys
It is not interchangeable with other amphotericin products
pk: Antifungal activity begins with the first infusions; clinical response over days
Plasma concentrations peak at the end of the infusion; high tissue uptake (liver, spleen)
Long and variable terminal half-life (roughly 7-10 hours initially, days with accumulation)
Store unopened vials at up to 25 C; after reconstitution use within recommended time, refrigerated
pearls: Liposomal form markedly reduces nephrotoxicity and infusion reactions versus conventional (deoxycholate) amphotericin
Different amphotericin B products are NOT interchangeable mg-for-mg - prescribe by specific product
Dilute only in 5% dextrose, never saline, and flush lines with dextrose
Preferred amphotericin formulation in pregnancy and in renal impairment
Monitor and replace potassium and magnesium; watch digoxin toxicity risk
missed: Administered as a scheduled hospital infusion; missed doses are managed by the clinical team. A delayed dose should be given as soon as practical without doubling up.
overdose: Overdose can cause cardiorespiratory arrest, severe electrolyte disturbance, and renal failure. There is no specific antidote; stop the infusion and provide supportive care with cardiac, renal, electrolyte, and haematological monitoring. Amphotericin B is not removed by haemodialysis.
